Listen to this article Share Advertisement Maritama Solar Tech, a Nigerian renewable energy company, has entered an exclusive partnership with YJC to distribute and deploy lithium batteries and inverter systems across Nigeria and West Africa.
The partnership will give households, businesses and industries access to YJC’s energy storage products, as Maritama seeks to expand its range of solar power solutions in a region where access to reliable electricity remains a concern.
The company said its decision to partner with YJC followed an assessment of the manufacturer’s technology, product specifications and long-term reliability. It added that its choice was influenced by the manufacturing and technological collaboration between YJC and BYD, through which both companies contribute hardware and software technologies to the development of YJC batteries.
According to the manufacturer, the batteries are designed to meet applicable European and American quality standards, offer more than 10,000 charge and discharge cycles under specified conditions, and come with warranties of up to 10 years.
YJC inverters are designed for power conversion, with warranties of five years or more on applicable models.
“We chose YJC because we want Maritama Solar Tech to be identified with quality, durability, technological innovation, and customer confidence,” the company said.
Maritama described the agreement as more than a distribution arrangement, stating that it represents a commitment to providing energy storage technology to customers across the region.
“It is a long-term commitment to bringing internationally competitive renewable energy technology to homes, businesses, and industries across Nigeria and West Africa,” the firm stated.
The YJC batteries use lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO₄) technology, which is designed for energy storage in residential, commercial and off-grid installations.
Their features include a built-in Battery Management System that protects against overcharging, excessive discharge, overcurrent and abnormal temperatures. The batteries also have IP65-rated casings designed to protect against dust and water.
The systems support parallel and stackable configurations, allowing users to increase storage capacity as their energy needs grow. Some models also offer cloud management and remote monitoring.
Maritama expects the batteries to arrive on or before November, with sales scheduled to begin within the week of their arrival. The company is targeting residential users, commercial establishments and industrial customers, while seeking partnerships with distributors and solar installers.
Beyond distributing the products, Maritama provides renewable energy services covering system design, installation, commissioning and maintenance. These services are intended to help customers select and operate systems based on their power requirements.
The company said its approach goes beyond selling batteries and inverters, with a focus on providing energy systems supported by technical assistance and customer service.
The partnership marks Maritama’s latest step towards expanding access to solar storage solutions in Nigeria and other West African markets. Its success will depend on product availability, technical support and the ability to meet the energy needs of customers seeking alternatives to conventional electricity supply.
